name: Script FFI C ABI compatibility requires a C wrapper fixture

input.source_text: module M { public fun run() -> Object { let lib = FFI.open("libfixture.so"); mut c = %{}; c[:convention] = :c; c[:parameters] = []; c[:result] = :i32; c[:errors] = :status; let bound = lib.bind(:c_wrapper, c); mut rust = %{}; rust[:convention] = :rust; rust[:parameters] = []; rust[:result] = :i32; rust[:errors] = :status; let refused = try { lib.bind(:rust_only, rust) } catch e { e }; [bound.bound?(:c_wrapper), refused] } } M.run()

applicability.reason: Supported. C049 supports the stable C ABI ONLY and requires an implementation-language library wanting script FFI access to export C-compatible wrapper symbols, so what the row observes is the SIGNATURE convention rather than which symbols a shared object happens to export. The earlier reason looked for a library exporting Rust-ABI symbols, but script FFI never reaches the symbol: `bind` validates the declared convention first, so a C-compatible wrapper binds while a signature naming another implementation language's convention is refused with IncompleteNativeSignatureError before any lookup. That is exactly C049's promise, and it makes no Rust ABI compatibility claim.
